overview.text: Plastic is not one chemical but a broad family of materials; most familiar examples are based on synthetic polymers, large molecules built from repeating monomer units. The polymer’s chain structure and chemistry help create different properties, so plastics can be flexible films, rigid containers, foams, or durable parts. Thermoplastics soften when heated and can be reshaped, while thermosetting plastics set into shapes that do not remelt reversibly. Their low weight, durability, and versatility make plastics useful in packaging, construction, transportation, and health care. But “plastic” does not name a single substance: products use many polymer types, and recycling systems may accept only some of them.

key_facts.text: Polymers are very large molecules made of repeating units called monomers; plastics are one group of polymeric materials.
Common plastic types include polyethylene terephthalate (PET), high- and low-density polyethylene (HDPE and LDPE), PVC, polypropylene (PP), and polystyrene (PS).
Thermoplastics can be melted and reshaped with heat; thermosetting plastics set irreversibly and do not remelt in the same way.
Plastic products are used in packaging, construction, transportation, and health care, among other fields.
Different plastics have different resin types, and some recycling systems accept only certain types.
